claim_verdicts.evidence: framework.dart L1062: 'The provided callback is immediately called synchronously.' L1068: 'causes the framework to schedule a [build] for this [State] object.' Source body ends '_element!.markNeedsBuild();'. refs ui/index.md L788: 'Calling `setState` marks this widget as dirty and schedules it to be rebuilt the next time your app needs to update the screen.'

framework.dart L1071-1073: 'If you just change the state directly without calling [setState], the framework might not schedule a [build] and the user interface for this subtree might not be updated to reflect the new state.' Lesson wording ('nothing asked Flutter to build again'; later build from another cause catches up) matches this.

setState doc: 'might impact the user interface in this subtree, which causes the framework to schedule a [build] for this [State] object'; implementation only calls _element!.markNeedsBuild() on this element. refs perf/best-practices.md L59-60: 'When `setState()` is called on a `State` object, all descendent widgets rebuild.' main.dart@stage-1: MaterialApp(home: ProductListScreen(...)) inside DonHangApp.build, so both are ancestors.

async.dart L614 'if (oldWidget.future == widget.future) { return; }'; L617-619 unsubscribe + inState(none); _subscribe then-callback 'setState(() { _snapshot = AsyncSnapshot<T>.withData(ConnectionState.done, data); })'; L664-665 sets inState(ConnectionState.waiting). Builder L46-47@stage-1: waiting -> CircularProgressIndicator. Round 3: new gloss 'shows a loading indicator while its Future is unfinished and the list once it completes' matches builder (error/empty branches not claimed otherwise).

login_screen.dart@stage-1 L23-27: 'Future<void> _submit() async { setState(() { _loading = true; _error = null; });' L57: 'if (_error != null) Text(_error!, style: ...)' L59-60: 'onPressed: _loading ? null : _submit, child: _loading ? const CircularProgressIndicator() : const Text('Sign in'),'.

setState doc: without setState the framework 'might not schedule a [build]'; any later build of _ProductListScreenState.build reads the already-assigned _products, and FutureBuilder.didUpdateWidget sees a different future, resubscribes and sets ConnectionState.waiting, then setState(done) on completion. Lesson no longer names the trigger (MediaQuery hint in source_hint unused), so claim holds as written.

Hedged opinion, supported: setState doc Performance considerations: 'causes the widget to rebuild, possibly triggering rebuilds for the entire subtree rooted at this widget'; best-practices.md: 'localize the `setState()` call to the part of the subtree whose UI actually needs to change.' Cost scales with the subtree rebuilt.

framework.dart L1062-1064: 'It must not return a future (the callback cannot be `async`), since then it would be unclear when the state was actually being set.' L1201-1205: 'final Object? result = fn() as dynamic; assert(() { if (result is Future) { throw FlutterError.fromParts([ErrorSummary('setState() callback argument returned a Future.')' - assert, debug only, matching 'while you are developing'. Arrow body returns the assignment value (the Future); block body without return yields null.

issues.text: 'API client' is not in what I know and not in Core concepts; 'API' is an acronym I have never been given. From the situation's GET /api/v1/products I can guess it is the thing that sends requests to the server, but I am guessing. The code line `widget.apiClient.fetchProducts()` rests on it.
issues.fix: Replace 'asks the screen's API client for the products again' with 'asks the object the screen uses to talk to the server (`apiClient`) for the products again'.
issues.quote: Inside it, `widget.apiClient.fetchProducts()` asks the screen's API client for the products again, and the new load is stored in `_products`.

issues.text: The code reaches the client through `widget.` from inside the State. The prereq told me the State is a separate object; nothing says the State can read its widget's fields through `widget`. I could follow the prose without it, but I paused on the prefix.
issues.fix: Add a short clause after the code-line sentence: '(`widget` is how a `State` reaches the fields of its own `ProductListScreen`)'.
issues.quote: Inside it, `widget.apiClient.fetchProducts()` asks the screen's API client

issues.text: `MaterialApp` first appears in section 4 with no explanation; I only learn in section 6 that `DonHangApp` returns it and it holds this screen. 'Above it' told me enough to keep going, so not blocking.
issues.fix: In section 4, change 'such as `DonHangApp` and `MaterialApp`' to 'such as `DonHangApp` and the `MaterialApp` it returns, which holds this screen'.
issues.quote: Widgets above it, such as `DonHangApp` and `MaterialApp`, are not built again

issues.text: I re-read this sentence twice: the inserted clause 'which comes after these lines' splits 'the sign-in request' from its verb 'starts', and then a second clause follows after the semicolon.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: 'The sign-in request comes after these lines. Because `setState` comes first in `_submit`, the state changes before that request starts, and the next time Flutter draws the screen the indicator shows while the request is in progress.'
issues.quote: The state changes before the sign-in request, which comes after these lines, starts, because `setState` comes first in `_submit`;
